reason: The cited evidence (E1) only shows that the HEA itself can be synthesized and has some thermal/irradiation stability; it provides no data on coating W particles, on W–Cu interfacial behavior, or on composite properties. The key premises about interfacial energy, wettability, void reduction, and performance improvements are entirely unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Refractory high-entropy alloy (CrFeTiTa)70W30 can be prepared and shows microstructural stability under annealing and irradiation.
A thin HEA interlayer on W particles can reduce interfacial energy differences and thermal expansion mismatches with Cu.
The HEA interlayer improves wettability and chemical compatibility, reducing void formation during sintering.
The graded interface stabilizes microstructure under irradiation, preserving mechanical durability and thermal conductivity.
The intervention will outperform conventional spark-plasma sintered W–Cu composites without an interlayer.
